items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had Elvin Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Forrest, and Joe Benjamin. I had a real good swinging band too... I kept that band together for about six years.

ctx.x: Well, you did record with Duke on that wonderful back to back…

That was one of my greatest moments. Norman Granz called me and wanted me to make this album. I said, oh man, did I want to do it, what a thrill. There was Johnny Hodges, I’d never played with him, never played with Duke. Jo Jones was on the record date and Joe Benjamin had played with my band when I first went to New York in the Birdland so I had played with him. But they were all beautiful friends of mine, but to be playing with Duke Ellington, gee whiz.
Do you remember that particular date, how it was to work with him in the studio?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano... Anyway, they opened up with me.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, you almost wanted to --

Yeah, wanted to go to New York, anyway. So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano, and oh, what's the drummer's name in New York, not Elvin because Elvin came latter. He played with Billy Eckstine for a long time. Good drummer.* Anyway, they opened up with me. And it was a fantastic night, you know.
And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.
